records.title: quantifier over a family of random variables
records.encoding:
module CT001
param mu : Real
param sigma : PositiveReal
var X : Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
require forall i : Natural . X[i] ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
records.diagnostics:
error HML-P204: unexpected '~' after require
  --> <input>:5:35
   5 | require forall i : Natural . X[i] ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
                                         ^
  help: HML-L1 permits one statement per line

controls.label: law targeting an indexed member
controls.source:
module CT001b
param mu : Real
param sigma : PositiveReal
var X : Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
law X[i] ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-P208: a law requires '~' between the variable and its distribution
  --> <input>:5:6
   5 | law X[i] ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
            ^
  note: '~' relates a RandomVariable[T] to a Distribution[T]
  help: law X ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
controls.why: `law` takes a bare identifier; there is no indexed law target

controls.label: the family itself exists and is indexable
controls.source:
module CT001c
var X : Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
param t : Real
require probability(X[1] > t) <= 1.0
controls.why: so the failure is the LAW, not the family

records.repair_note: a law must be able to sit under a binder: either `law` becomes an expression, or a `for each i : T` statement binder is added. Neither is expressible by adding one more Expr subclass.
records.note: `law`/`prior`/`likelihood` are STATEMENTS and `forall` is an EXPRESSION, so a law can never appear under a binder. `law X[i] ~ ...` is refused at the parser (HML-P208: the target must be an identifier). The family of random variables does exist -- Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N] indexes fine and yields events -- so what is missing is exclusively the ability to attach a distributional law under a quantifier.
control_anomalies: law targeting an indexed member

records.title: quantifier over matrices with a shape hypothesis
records.encoding:
module CT002
require forall A : Matrix[Real, N, N] . forall x : Vector[Real, N] . not (x = x) or (x @ (A @ x)) > 0.0

controls.label: shape disagreement under the binder is caught
controls.source:
module CT002b
require forall A : Matrix[Real, N, N] . forall x : Vector[Real, M] . (x @ (A @ x)) > 0.0
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T434: inner dimensions do not agree in a matrix-vector product
  --> <input>:2:75
   2 | require forall A : Matrix[Real, N, N] . forall x : Vector[Real, M] . (x @ (A @ x)) > 0.0
                                                                                 ^^^^^^^
  found:    Vector[Real, M]
  expected: Vector[..., N]
controls.why: symbolic extents must be checked, not ignored

records.note: Shape checking runs under the binder on symbolic extents. Symmetry of A is not expressible as a type (no Sym(n)); it is a declared degradation, not a silent one, and the specimen's stated hard part -- symbolic shape agreement under a binder -- holds.

records.title: quantifier over a dimensionful domain
records.encoding:
module CT003
param g : Quantity[Length / Time^2]
require forall L : Quantity[Length] . sqrt(L / g) = sqrt(L / g)
records.diagnostics:
error HML-T427: the argument of sqrt has the wrong type
  --> <input>:3:44
   3 | require forall L : Quantity[Length] . sqrt(L / g) = sqrt(L / g)
                                                  ^^^^^
  found:    Quantity[Time^2]
  expected: NonNegativeReal

error HML-T427: the argument of sqrt has the wrong type
  --> <input>:3:58
   3 | require forall L : Quantity[Length] . sqrt(L / g) = sqrt(L / g)
                                                                ^^^^^
  found:    Quantity[Time^2]
  expected: NonNegativeReal

controls.label: quantifying over a dimensionful domain alone
controls.source:
module CT003b
require forall L : Quantity[Length] . L >= L
controls.why: the binder itself is fine; the failure is downstream

controls.label: a dimensionful interval endpoint
controls.source:
module CT003c
const zero_m : Quantity[Length] = 0.0
require zero_m = zero_m
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T402: the declared type of 'zero_m' requires Quantity[Length]
  --> <input>:2:35
   2 | const zero_m : Quantity[Length] = 0.0
                                         ^^^
  found:    NonNegativeReal
  expected: Quantity[Length]
  help: the dimensions differ: Dimensionless vs Length; convert one side
controls.why: there is no unit-carrying literal, so [0 m, 10 m] is unwritable

records.repair_note: a Quantity overload for `sqrt` that halves the dimension exponents (Dimension already stores Fraction exponents), plus a unit-carrying literal -- a field on Literal and a lexer rule.
records.note: Two independent breakages. (a) `sqrt` is typed `NonNegativeReal -> NonNegativeReal`; it has no Quantity overload, so the half-dimension the specimen is about cannot be taken at all -- HML-T427. (b) There is no dimensionful literal, so the interval [0 m, 10 m] has no surface form (HML-T402). The quantifier/Quantity composition itself works.
control_anomalies: a dimensionful interval endpoint

records.title: distribution parameters carrying units
records.encoding:
module CT004
param mu : Quantity[Length]
param sigma : Quantity[Length]
rv H : RandomVariable[Quantity[Length]]
law H ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
records.diagnostics:
error HML-T413: the 'location' role of Normal requires Real
  --> <input>:5:28
   5 | law H ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
                                  ^^
  found:    Quantity[Length]
  expected: Real
  note: scale is the standard deviation, not the variance
  help: declare 'mu : Real'

error HML-T413: the 'scale' role of Normal requires PositiveReal
  --> <input>:5:41
   5 | law H ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
                                               ^^^^^
  found:    Quantity[Length]
  expected: PositiveReal
  note: scale is the standard deviation, not the variance
  help: declare 'sigma : PositiveReal'

error HML-T411: the support of Normal does not inhabit the declared type of 'H'
  --> <input>:5:1
   5 | law H ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  found:    support Real
  expected: Quantity[Length]
  note: Normal is supported on Real
  help: declare 'H : Real', or choose a family whose support is Quantity[Length]

controls.label: unitless variant
controls.source:
module CT004b
param mu : Real
param sigma : PositiveReal
rv H : RandomVariable[Real]
law H ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := sigma)
controls.why: the same statement without units compiles, isolating the unit as the cause

records.repair_note: make DistributionSpec dimension-parametric: one dimension variable on the support and on the location/scale roles.
records.note: Every distribution family in the registry fixes its support and its role types to unrefined scalars (Normal: location Real, scale PositiveReal, support Real). `DistributionSpec` has no dimension variable, so RandomVariable does not compose with Quantity anywhere. Three diagnostics fire at once: HML-T413 on both roles and HML-T411 on the support.

records.title: minimising an expectation
records.encoding:
module CT005
var A : Set[Real]
param a : Real
rv S : RandomVariable[Real]
law S ~ Normal(location := 0.0, scale := 1.0)
def loss(u : Real, s : Real) : Real := u * s
require a in A
minimise expectation(loss(a, S))

facts.description: the objective is a value, not a random variable (the expectation really integrated S out)

records.note: Two binders of different kinds nest correctly: the measurable lifting rule makes `loss(a, S)` a RandomVariable[Real], `expectation` integrates S out and returns Real, and `a` stays a free parameter. The feasible-set membership is carried by a separate `require`, because `minimise` has no binder of its own.

records.title: matrix with a symbolic structural constraint
records.encoding:
module CT006
var Sigma : Matrix[Real, N, N]
var x : Vector[Real, N]
var b : Vector[Real, N]
require forall z : Vector[Real, N] . (z @ (Sigma @ z)) > 0.0
require (Sigma @ x) = b
solve Sigma

controls.label: a shape-incompatible equation is caught
controls.source:
module CT006b
var Sigma : Matrix[Real, N, N]
var x : Vector[Real, N]
var b : Vector[Real, M]
require (Sigma @ x) = b
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T429: these operands are not comparable
  --> <input>:5:9
   5 | require (Sigma @ x) = b
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  found:    Vector[Real, M]
  expected: Vector[Real, N]

records.note: The unknown carries its shape, the positive-definiteness constraint is a quantified proposition attached to the unknown rather than checked against a value, and `solve` marks it as the thing to be found.

records.title: a function whose value is a distribution
records.encoding:
module CT007
param sigma : PositiveReal
var f : Function[Real -> Real]
def k(x : Real) : Distribution[Real] := Normal(location := f(x), scale := sigma)

controls.label: a distribution is not a value of its support
controls.source:
module CT007b
const d : Distribution[Real] = 1.0
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T402: the declared type of 'd' requires Distribution[Real]
  --> <input>:2:32
   2 | const d : Distribution[Real] = 1.0
                                      ^^^
  found:    PositiveReal
  expected: Distribution[Real]
  help: supply an expression of type Distribution[Real] for the declared type of 'd'

records.note: Dist(R) exists as a type distinct from R and survives being a codomain.

records.title: indexed family of RVs with index-dependent parameters
records.encoding:
module CT008
param beta : Real
param sigma : PositiveReal
var x : Vector[Real, N]
var Y : Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
require forall i : Natural . forall j : Natural . not (i = j) => independent(Y[i], Y[j])
require forall i : Natural . Y[i] ~ Normal(location := beta * x[i], scale := sigma)
records.diagnostics:
error HML-P204: unexpected '~' after require
  --> <input>:7:35
   7 | require forall i : Natural . Y[i] ~ Normal(location := beta * x[i], scale := sigma)
                                         ^
  help: HML-L1 permits one statement per line

controls.label: the family-level independence claim alone
controls.source:
module CT008b
var Y : Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
require forall i : Natural . forall j : Natural . not (i = j) => independent(Y[i], Y[j])
controls.why: family-level independence over an index composes

controls.label: the per-index law alone
controls.source:
module CT008c
param beta : Real
param sigma : PositiveReal
var x : Vector[Real, N]
var Y : Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
law Y ~ Normal(location := beta, scale := sigma)
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T411: the support of Normal does not inhabit the declared type of 'Y'
  --> <input>:6:1
   6 | law Y ~ Normal(location := beta, scale := sigma)
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  found:    support Real
  expected: Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
  note: Normal is supported on Real
  help: declare 'Y : Real', or choose a family whose support is Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
controls.why: and the per-index law does not

records.repair_note: the same wall as CT-001.
records.note: Exactly CT-001's wall, isolated: the family-level property (independence over a quantified index pair) composes and compiles clean; the index-level property (a law per i) has no surface form because `law` is a statement and cannot sit under a binder, and its target must be an identifier.
control_anomalies: the per-index law alone

records.title: gradient of an expectation whose measure depends on the parameter
records.encoding:
module CT009
param theta : Real
rv Z : RandomVariable[Real]
law Z | theta ~ Normal(location := theta, scale := 1.0)
def f(z : Real) : Real := z * z
def obj := derivative(expectation(f(Z)), theta : Real)

controls.label: differentiating against a fresh name is accepted, and is not the statement
controls.source:
module CT009b
param theta : Real
rv Z : RandomVariable[Real]
law Z | theta ~ Normal(location := theta, scale := 1.0)
def f(z : Real) : Real := z * z
def obj := derivative(expectation(f(Z)), th : Real)
controls.why: the binder `th` occurs nowhere in the body; the theta-dependence is gone and nothing warns

records.repair_note: differentiating with respect to an EXISTING symbol needs either binder-by- reference or abstraction plus application; binder-always-fresh plus D-006 makes it unreachable.
records.note: `derivative` always introduces a FRESH binder, and D-006 forbids shadowing, so differentiating with respect to a symbol that already exists is impossible: HML-N302. The only accepted spelling binds a name that does not occur in the body, which silently states the derivative of a constant. This is the clearest measured case of the binder design being the obstacle rather than the type rules.

records.title: definite integral carrying units
records.encoding:
module CT010
param t0 : Quantity[Time]
param t1 : Quantity[Time]
var P : Function[Quantity[Time] -> Quantity[Mass * Length^2 / Time^3]]
def En := integral(P(t), t : Quantity[Time], t0, t1)

controls.label: claiming the integral is still in watts is refused
controls.source:
module CT010b
param t0 : Quantity[Time]
param t1 : Quantity[Time]
var P : Function[Quantity[Time] -> Quantity[Mass * Length^2 / Time^3]]
param W : Quantity[Mass * Length^2 / Time^3]
def En := integral(P(t), t : Quantity[Time], t0, t1)
require En = W
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-D502: cannot compare quantities with different dimensions
  --> <input>:7:9
   7 | require En = W
               ^^^^^^
  found:    Length^2 * Mass / Time^3
  expected: Length^2 * Mass / Time^2
  note: comparison requires dimensional equality
controls.why: HML-D502 proves the unit was really acquired, not merely printed

facts.description: the integral multiplied by the binder's dimension: W*s = J

records.note: The differential contributes its unit factor and the checker enforces it. The endpoints must be declared parameters rather than written `0 s`, because HML has no unit-carrying literal (see CT-003 control c); that is a standalone gap in NUM.INTERVAL_DOMAIN, not a composition failure, and it is recorded as such.

records.title: local assumption inside a function body

controls.label: nothing leaks to a sibling scope
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T427: the argument of log has the wrong type
  --> <input>:4:14
   4 | def h := log(z)
                    ^
  found:    Real
  expected: PositiveReal
controls.why: the positivity of g's parameter must not license log(z)

controls.label: a module-level assume does discharge the obligation for that symbol
controls.source:
module CT011c
param r : Real
assume r > 0.0
def y := log(r)
controls.why: D-028's refinement environment, working

records.note: The hypothesis is carried by the parameter's declared refinement, is in force exactly inside the body, discharges log's definedness obligation, and does not leak. D-028 additionally makes a module-level `assume` on a bare reference discharge the same obligation -- this specimen's ancestor COMP.LOCAL_ASSUMPTION_IN_SCOPE was a documented failure in AUDIT_RERUN §4 and now passes.

records.title: constraint scoped to a subset of an index set
records.encoding:
module CT012
var A : Set[Natural]
var x : Vector[Real, N]
var c : Vector[Real, N]
require forall i : Natural . i in A => x[i] <= c[i]

facts.description: the guard is inside the quantifier body, not hoisted out of it

records.note: The bounded quantifier is a guarded implication under one binder; the feasible set is not silently widened to all of I.

records.title: objective over derived state
records.encoding:
module CT013
param x : Real
def Mf(u : Real) : Real := u * u
def y := Mf(x)
def C(v : Real) : Real := v + 1.0
minimise C(y)

facts.description: y is a definition (derived), not a declaration (free)

records.note: `def` and `param` are different AST kinds and stay different through canonicalisation, so the given/derived distinction the specimen turns on is structural rather than conventional.

records.title: tensor appearing inside a proposition
records.encoding:
module CT014
var T : Tensor[Real, 2, 3, 4]
require forall i : Natural . forall j : Natural . forall k : Natural . T[i, j, k] = T[j, i, k]

controls.label: a literal index outside the declared extent
controls.source:
module CT014b
var T : Tensor[Real, 2, 3, 4]
require T[99, 0, 0] = T[0, 0, 0]
controls.why: extents are declared; a literal 99 into a 2 should not pass

facts.description: index order is not normalised away: T_ijk = T_jik differs from T_ijk = T_ijk

records.repair_note: range-check literal indices against the declared extents; the extents are already in the type.
records.note: The composition the specimen asks for works: the index variables are genuine logical binders and simultaneously tensor indices, and the symmetry claim keeps its own canonical identity. But literal indices are never range-checked against the declared extents -- `T[99,0,0]` on a Tensor[Real,2,3,4] compiles clean. That is an implementation gap in `Index` typing, not a design limit: the extents are already in the type.
control_anomalies: a literal index outside the declared extent

records.title: quantifier alternation order: uniform versus pointwise
records.encoding:
module CT015
var f : Function[Real -> Real]
require forall e : PositiveReal . exists d : PositiveReal . forall x : Real . forall y : Real . abs(x - y) < d => abs(f(x) - f(y)) < e

facts.description: uniform continuity and pointwise continuity have different canonical hashes
alpha-renaming does not change the hash

records.note: Quantifier order is structural; nothing sorts or hoists binders. This is HML's strongest measured property and it survives a four-binder alternation.

records.title: approximate value inside a proof obligation
records.encoding:
module CT016
var A : Matrix[Real, 3, 3]
param d : Real
assume d ~ 0.00000000000001
require not (d = 0.0)
records.diagnostics:
error HML-P204: unexpected '~' after assume
  --> <input>:4:10
   4 | assume d ~ 0.00000000000001
                ^
  help: HML-L1 permits one statement per line

controls.label: the exact-equality spelling is accepted, i.e. ~ collapses to =
controls.source:
module CT016b
param d : Real
assume d = 0.00000000000001
require not (d = 0.0)
controls.why: an approximate determinant discharges an exact non-zeroness claim, because the approximation cannot be marked

records.repair_note: one approximation marker -- an operator and one node -- closes CT-016, CT-042 and CT-044 together.
records.note: There is no approximation marker in HML-L1. `~` is reserved for distributed-as and has no expression production; the lexer's operator set contains no `≈`. `v1/epistemic.py` defines APPROXIMATELY_EQUAL but that layer is not reachable from the L1 grammar. The atom NUMER.APPROXIMATION_MARKER is absent standalone, so the composition cannot be attempted. The control shows the consequence: written with `=`, the approximate value discharges the exact obligation.

records.title: matrix-valued random variable with a structural constraint
records.encoding:
module CT017
param nu : PositiveReal
var Psi : Matrix[Real, P, P]
rv Sigma : RandomVariable[Matrix[Real, P, P]]
law Sigma ~ InverseWishart(degrees_of_freedom := nu, scale := Psi)
records.diagnostics:
error HML-T412: unknown distribution family 'InverseWishart'
  --> <input>:5:13
   5 | law Sigma ~ InverseWishart(degrees_of_freedom := nu, scale := Psi)
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  note: v0 implements a deliberately small registry; see src/hamiltonian_lang/type_system/distributions.py
  help: known families include: InverseGamma, Bernoulli, Beta

controls.label: the matrix-valued random variable itself is fine
controls.source:
module CT017b
rv Sigma : RandomVariable[Matrix[Real, P, P]]
param t : Real
require probability(Sigma = Sigma) >= 0.0
controls.why: so the failure is the family, not the carrier type

records.repair_note: one matrix-supported family in the registry, with a support constraint.
records.note: HML-T412: no matrix-supported family exists in the registry (17 families, all scalar- or vector-supported). The carrier type RandomVariable[Matrix[...]] is accepted, so shape and randomness compose; what is absent is any distribution whose support is a constrained matrix manifold, and there is no way to state 'every draw is SPD' as a property of the law rather than of a realisation.

records.title: conditional expectation given a sigma-algebra
records.encoding:
module CT018
rv X : RandomVariable[Real]
var G : Set[Set[Real]]
def c := expectation(X | G)

facts.description: E[X | G] must be a G-measurable RANDOM VARIABLE, not a value

records.repair_note: a sigma-algebra type in types.py and one clause in the moment rule; no expression node changes.
records.note: This compiles clean and is wrong. `expectation(X | G)` types as `Real` -- byte-identical in type to the unconditional `expectation(X)` -- because the moment rule reads 'conditioning on something non-random yields a value'. That rule is right for a parameter and wrong for a sigma-algebra: E[X|G] is the almost-surely unique G-measurable random variable. There is no sigma-algebra type, no measurability predicate and no a.s. qualifier, so nothing catches it. The two expressions do hash differently, so the conditioning set is stored -- the loss is in the TYPE, which is the part downstream consumers read.

records.title: piecewise function with a domain partition
records.encoding:
module CT019
var x : Real
def f := if x >= 0.0 then x * x else -x
records.diagnostics:
error HML-P204: unexpected 'x' after definition
  --> <input>:3:13
   3 | def f := if x >= 0.0 then x * x else -x
                   ^
  help: HML-L1 permits one statement per line

controls.label: the guarded-implication workaround compiles
controls.source:
module CT019b
var f : Function[Real -> Real]
require forall u : Real . u >= 0.0 => f(u) = u * u
require forall u : Real . u < 0.0 => f(u) = -u

controls.label: but a branch guard is NOT a local assumption
controls.source:
module CT019c
var f : Function[Real -> Real]
require forall u : Real . u > 0.0 => f(u) = log(u)
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T427: the argument of log has the wrong type
  --> <input>:3:49
   3 | require forall u : Real . u > 0.0 => f(u) = log(u)
                                                       ^
  found:    Real
  expected: PositiveReal
controls.why: the specimen requires each branch to carry its guard as a hypothesis; the guard does not enter the refinement environment

records.repair_note: one conditional / piecewise expression form.
records.note: No conditional expression exists: `if` is not a keyword and HML-P204 fires at the first token. The two-`require` workaround states the graph but loses both properties the specimen names -- exhaustiveness and disjointness are unchecked, and control c proves the guard does not discharge the branch's obligations, because D-028's refinement environment is keyed on module-level `assume` over a bare Ref and does not descend into an implication's antecedent.
control_anomalies: but a branch guard is NOT a local assumption

records.title: statement quantifying over functions
records.encoding:
module CT020
var I : Set[Real]
require forall f : Function[Real -> Real] . continuous(f, on := I) and (forall x : Real . x in I => f(x) in I) => exists c : Real . c in I and f(c) = c

facts.description: the existential really is inside the universal, not hoisted

records.note: Second-order quantification works: the binder's domain may be a function type, the continuity restriction composes with a set-valued domain, and the inner existential keeps its position. The closed unit interval is carried as a `Set[Real]` guard rather than a type, because HML has no interval types -- a declared degradation, and the same one every system without refinement-typed intervals would report.

records.title: probability of a quantified event
records.encoding:
module CT021
var X : Vector[RandomVariable[Real], N]
param t : Real
param alpha : Probability
require probability(exists i : Natural . X[i] > t) <= alpha

controls.label: a quantified body over FIXED quantities is refused inside probability
controls.source:
module CT021b
param y : Real
param t : Real
param alpha : Probability
require probability(exists i : Natural . y > t) <= alpha
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-T482: the argument of 'probability' is a proposition, not an event
  --> <input>:5:21
   5 | require probability(exists i : Natural . y > t) <= alpha
                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  found:    Proposition
  expected: Event
  note: a proposition over fixed quantities is true or false, so its probability is 0 or 1 and asking for it states nothing
  help: declare the quantities it mentions as 'rv X : RandomVariable[...]' so the formula denotes an event
controls.why: HML-T482: the probability of a proposition is 0 or 1 and states nothing

facts.description: the quantified body really denotes an event, not a proposition

records.note: The quantifier lives inside the probability operator and its body is classified as an Event because the family members are random. The Event/Proposition split is exactly the distinction the specimen says is load-bearing, and the control shows it is enforced in both directions.

records.title: hierarchical model with an acyclic dependency structure
records.encoding:
module CT022
param mu : Real
prior mu ~ Normal(location := 0.0, scale := 10.0)
rv X : RandomVariable[Real]
law X | mu ~ Normal(location := mu, scale := 1.0)

controls.label: a CYCLIC variant must be rejected
controls.source:
module CT022b
param a : Real
param b : Real
prior a ~ Normal(location := b, scale := 1.0)
prior b ~ Normal(location := a, scale := 1.0)
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-S607: circular probability law: a -> b -> a
  --> <input>:4:1
   4 | prior a ~ Normal(location := b, scale := 1.0)
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  note: a set of mutually dependent laws specifies no joint distribution: there is no density to factor and nothing to infer from
  note: detected because module scope is order-independent (D-008), which is exactly what makes such a cycle expressible
  help: break the cycle -- give one of these symbols a law that does not depend on the others, or declare it as a 'param'
controls.why: the specimen's stated requirement: 'must reject a cyclic variant'

records.repair_note: one acyclicity pass over the law graph, which is already present in LawStmt.given and the DistExpr role arguments.
records.note: The dual role composes -- `mu` is the variate of one law and a role argument of another, and the checker accepts it. But `a ~ Normal(mean := b)` together with `b ~ Normal(mean := a)` compiles clean: no acyclicity check exists anywhere. The dependency edges are already in `LawStmt.given` and in the DistExpr role arguments, so this is a missing pass, not a missing representation -- no AST change would be needed to fix it.

records.title: conditioning versus intervening
records.encoding:
module CT023
rv R : RandomVariable[Bool]
rv T : RandomVariable[Bool]
require probability(R | do(T)) != probability(R | T)
records.diagnostics:
error HML-N306: 'do' is not a known function
  --> <input>:4:25
   4 | require probability(R | do(T)) != probability(R | T)
                               ^^^^^
  help: did you mean 'R'?

controls.label: observational conditioning alone is fine
controls.source:
module CT023b
rv R : RandomVariable[Bool]
rv T : RandomVariable[Bool]
require probability(R = true | T = true) >= 0.0

controls.label: and causation is at least kept apart from correlation
controls.source:
module CT023c
rv R : RandomVariable[Bool]
rv T : RandomVariable[Bool]

records.title: optimisation over a distribution
records.encoding:
module CT046
var Q : Set[Distribution[Real]]
var p : Distribution[Real]
var q : Distribution[Real]
var kl : Function[Distribution[Real], Distribution[Real] -> NonNegativeReal]
require q in Q
minimise kl(q, p)
solve q

facts.description: KL(q||p) and KL(p||q) are canonically different objects

records.note: The decision variable really is a Distribution[Real] -- a first-class object that the type system keeps apart from its support -- the family is a Set[Distribution[Real]], and argument order is preserved so the asymmetry cannot be lost by an accidental swap. The degradation: `kl` is an uninterpreted declared function, and its two arguments are POSITIONAL, so D-003's role labelling -- the mechanism that would have named the asymmetry -- is not available for user-declared functions.

records.title: sup versus max in an optimisation conclusion

controls.label: a sup/inf primitive
controls.diagnostics:
error HML-N306: 'infimum' is not a known function
  --> <input>:3:10
   3 | def i := infimum(S)
                ^^^^^^^^^^
  help: declare it first, e.g. 'param infimum : Real'
controls.why: HML-N306: ANA.SUP_INF has no builtin; the meaning is recoverable by comprehension, so this is vocabulary and not part of the gate

facts.description: the set of lower bounds is a Set, and no minimiser is asserted

records.note: There is no `inf`/`sup` primitive, but the mathematics is expressible by comprehension -- the set of lower bounds -- and the non-attainment claim is expressible as a quantified negation. Crucially, `minimise` in HML declares an objective and does not assert that a minimiser exists, so the dangerous error the specimen guards against is not committed. Degraded on vocabulary, not on meaning.
